Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the line segment shown above.
question.:question/worked-solution:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s=L.
$$

In this case, the path $C$ is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose legs have lengths $3$ and $4.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s=5.
$$

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s=L.

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\sqrt{{\frac{7}{4}}^{2}+{\frac{10}{3}}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{49}{16}+\frac{100}{9}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2041}{144}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2041}}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s=\frac{\sqrt{2041}}{12}.
$$
